Only two measurements enter: GGG, measured in the laboratory, and Λ\LambdaΛ, which Planck’s H0H_0H0​ and ΩΛ\Omega_\LambdaΩΛ​ give.

This section derives the horizon that Sec. II counted, so we state the order in which the argument runs. Section II counted the largest rings and gave every observer’s horizon one bit for each; no solution of any equation was used. Its count of a sphere’s strings, Eq. (8), uses the space this section finds, and Einstein’s equations do not need it. Of the register, their form needs only that the entropy density is positive and, being a law, the same on every horizon by the symmetry of space. Their constant GGG needs the density’s value, the horizon’s entropy over its area (Sec. III). This section finds that area from the form of the equations, the symmetry of space, and the rings, with cited geometry and without the value of η\etaη (Sec. II). Their solution without a mass has, in its space at an instant, closed geodesics of one length, a largest ring’s, so the count left no ring out. Had that space allowed shorter rings, they would have carried bits the count did not include, and the equations would not describe the space they produce. The solution with a mass, Schwarzschild–de Sitter, has at its horizons circles shorter than a largest ring: the great circles of the cosmological horizon, of LM=L−2α/ln⁡2L_M = L - 2\alpha/\ln2LM​=L−2α/ln2 cells (Sec. IV C), and, for a black hole, of its own horizon, of L′=4πGM/c2ℓcL' = 4\pi GM/c^2\lcL′=4πGM/c2ℓc​ cells. Whether they are rings, the shorter rings Postulate 1 allows, outside the count of Postulate 2, no derivation of the paper needs; their cells lie on largest rings as every cell does. To leading order, the horizon with the mass inside holds LM2/4L_M^2/4LM2​/4 bits by the area law (Sec. IV C), and the black hole’s holds (L′2/4)ln⁡2=πrs2/ℓP2=A/4ℓP2(L'^2/4)\ln2 = \pi r_s^2/\ell_P^2 = A/4\ell_P^2(L′2/4)ln2=πrs2​/ℓP2​=A/4ℓP2​, with rs=2GM/c2r_s = 2GM/c^2rs​=2GM/c2 its radius. The register’s rings stay the largest rings, on which a body’s strings lie and which carry the entropy inside its horizon (Secs. II, IV C), and 2N≤L2^N\le L2N≤L holds for every string (Sec. IV A). The actual universe, with its matter, is not the solution without a mass, nor is its matter a mass at rest inside a horizon, the case of Eq. (17): it is neither at rest nor a point mass. Even counted as one, it would lie beyond the limit up to which the solution has a horizon at all (Appendix A). So nothing is claimed here for the entropy of the horizon today: every horizon statement of the paper concerns the de Sitter state the universe approaches, with expansion rate H∞=H0ΩΛH_\infty = H_0\sqrt{\Omega_\Lambda}H∞​=H0​ΩΛ​​ (Appendix A), and Sec. II counts that horizon. A largest ring, though, has LLL cells today as in that state: LLL is a constant. The count of Sec. IV C, L/4L/4L/4 cells to the de Sitter horizon, therefore holds for a body observed today. How a largest ring closes in the manifold of a universe with matter is beyond the scope of this paper. We read such a ring as a closed geodesic of the solution without a mass. The paper uses that solution for four things: the value of η\etaη, which is a law (Sec. III C); the constant Λ\LambdaΛ, with the surface gravity and the temperature of its horizon; the count of Eq. (8); and the vacuum’s energy (below). Each is a law or a constant of the equations: a law is a function of the register (Sec. II), which matter, a state of its strings, leaves as it is; Λ\LambdaΛ is one constant on the whole spacetime (Sec. III); and Einstein’s equations are derived with matter (Sec. III).

The closed ring also gives the vacuum its energy. An observer’s horizon holds one bit for each ring, Eq. (7), at the temperature Ec/L\Ec/LEc​/L, Eq. (11), so its heat, entropy times temperature, is one Landauer energy for each string; to leading order,

and the equality with c4RΛ/2Gc^4\RL/2Gc4RΛ​/2G uses Eq. (14). The horizon is the de Sitter one derived above, constant in time, as observation requires: LLL and the cell are constants (Postulate 1), so by Eq. (5) its radius is constant. Eqs. (5) and (14), at one bit per ring, tie the cell to the radius and GGG to its square: were the horizon the Hubble radius RH=c/HR_H = c/HRH​=c/H with LLL fixed, G∝RH2G\propto R_H^2G∝RH2​ would drift at G˙/G=2H(1+q)≈6.5×10−11\dot G/G = 2H(1+q)\approx6.5\times10^{-11}G˙/G=2H(1+q)≈6.5×10−11 yr−1^{-1}−1, about 650 times the lunar-laser-ranging bound [81], with q≈−0.53q\approx-0.53q≈−0.53 the present deceleration parameter. With RΛ\RLRΛ​ constant, and ccc, ℏ\hbarℏ and kBk_BkB​ fixed by the definition of the SI units [82], GGG, a0a_0a0​, and Λ\LambdaΛ are all constant, as Eq. (29) requires, and since every observer’s horizon has the same radius, LLL is observer-independent.

E. Heat and energy of the strings

Every physical quantity is defined by qubits (Postulate 1), and the qubits are strings, one on each ring (Sec. II), so the rings hold all the energy there is. The shift is a translation along the ring, which leaves a string of one sense as it is, since every cell of it holds the same bit, and nothing else happens to a free string (Postulate 1): the tick multiplies the string of all 1s by a factor. Reversing the direction of the ring turns it into the string of all −1-1−1s, and no law depends on that direction (Postulate 2), so the tick multiplies that string by the same factor. The tick is linear, so it multiplies every state of the string by that one factor, and the string’s phase, its position (Postulate 1), does not change. By the definition of energy (Sec. II) the factor is e−iEtc/ℏe^{-iE\tc/\hbar}e−iEtc​/ℏ, with EEE the string’s energy: one energy for all the string’s states, whose global phase decreases by Eτ/ℏE\tau/\hbarEτ/ℏ in a time τ\tauτ. Since the energy is one for all the string’s states, it adds no state: each string remains one qubit, with one bit of entropy (Postulate 1).

The postulates fix no value for EEE. It grows with the mass the string holds, so it differs from string to string and can take any value from zero up. Since the energy adds no state and equal amounts of mass add equal energies, no value counts more than another apart from its thermal weight. Thermodynamics distributes a system over its distinguishable configurations, and the distribution of most entropy at a given mean energy is the Gibbs distribution. It enters here twice. Over a free string’s two senses, which have one energy, it is 1/21/21/2, 1/21/21/2 at every temperature: one bit, whatever energy the string holds. Over the strings it spreads the energies they hold, at the horizon’s temperature (Sec. III): the value EEE carries the weight e−E/kBTdSe^{-E/k_BT_{\rm dS}}e−E/kB​TdS​, and the average energy of a string is

⟨E⟩=∫0∞E e−E/kBTdS dE∫0∞e−E/kBTdS dE=kBTdS.\langle E\rangle = \frac{\int_0^\infty E\,e^{-E/k_BT_{\rm dS}}\,dE}{\int_0^\infty e^{-E/k_BT_{\rm dS}}\,dE} = k_BT_{\rm dS} .⟨E⟩=∫0∞​e−E/kB​TdS​dE∫0∞​Ee−E/kB​TdS​dE​=kB​TdS​.
(33)

If the energy comes in equal steps ϵ\epsilonϵ instead, the average is ϵ/(eϵ/kBTdS−1)\epsilon/(e^{\epsilon/k_BT_{\rm dS}}-1)ϵ/(eϵ/kB​TdS​−1), below kBTdSk_BT_{\rm dS}kB​TdS​ by less than one step. By Eq. (10) the average is ℏ\hbarℏ over the lap time of a largest ring: on average a string’s global phase decreases by one radian in LLL ticks, as in Palmer’s Eq. (4) read backward.

The spread is a difference between strings, not a change in time: the energies the strings hold do not change (Sec. III), since this paper treats matter that stays put (Sec. II). A horizon’s entropy counts what can change in its strings, which in a free string is the sense alone. The entropy of the spread is that of a distribution over the strings and adds nothing to the horizon’s. The results use the spread through its average and, in Sec. IV C, through the fraction of the strings above a given energy.

The strings’ heat is the horizon’s temperature times their one bit each, kBTdSln⁡2k_BT_{\rm dS}\ln2kB​TdS​ln2 per string, the fraction ln⁡2\ln2ln2 of the average energy; it is the energy that Sec. IV D found for the vacuum, one Landauer energy per string. The rest of the average, the fraction 1−ln⁡2=0.3071-\ln2 = 0.3071−ln2=0.307, is matter. The split is of the strings’ energy as a whole, not string by string. Every physical quantity is defined by qubits (Postulate 1), so the energy inside the horizon is the strings’ and nothing else’s: kBTdSk_BT_{\rm dS}kB​TdS​ per string on average, of which the vacuum’s is the fraction ln⁡2\ln2ln2. The vacuum’s share of the energy is therefore ΩΛ=ln⁡2=0.693\Omega_\Lambda = \ln2 = 0.693ΩΛ​=ln2=0.693. Planck’s value is 0.685±0.0070.685\pm0.0070.685±0.007 [77], 1.2σ1.2\sigma1.2σ lower, and DESI’s baryon acoustic oscillations alone give 0.7025±0.00860.7025\pm0.00860.7025±0.0086 [83], 1.1σ1.1\sigma1.1σ higher. Interactions between strings, rare in this epoch, would move this split slightly; this paper does not treat them. In earlier epochs interactions were not rare (Sec. II), and a Gibbs distribution, which is static, does not describe the strings’ energies then. How far back the split holds is left to a later paper. Section IV C uses the matter in the average energy as the unit of a body’s share.

V. Does LLL Hold?

Table II collects the results. Two scales bear on LLL, each with the cell from the measured GGG, and each gives a value. The cosmological scale, through the size of the de Sitter horizon, gives 4.37×10614.37\times10^{61}4.37×1061. The galactic scale, through the measured a0a_0a0​ and Eq. (28), gives (4.37±0.87)×1061(4.37\pm0.87)\times10^{61}(4.37±0.87)×1061 with McGaugh’s a0a_0a0​ and (4.40±0.37)×1061(4.40\pm0.37)\times10^{61}(4.40±0.37)×1061 with Desmond’s; all give log⁡2L=204.8\log_2L = 204.8log2​L=204.8 and Nmax⁡=204N_{\max} = 204Nmax​=204. The two come from scales five orders of magnitude apart, and their agreement does not test the power of ten, which both take from the cell; ℓc\lcℓc​ cancels in the ratio Lgal/LcosL_{\rm gal}/L_{\rm cos}Lgal​/Lcos​, the derived a0a_0a0​ over the measured one. It tests the coefficient: that a0RΛ/c2a_0\RL/c^2a0​RΛ​/c2 is (1−ln⁡2)/2ln⁡2=0.221(1-\ln2)/2\ln2 = 0.221(1−ln2)/2ln2=0.221, where the measurements give 0.22±0.040.22\pm0.040.22±0.04 and 0.22±0.020.22\pm0.020.22±0.02.

The scale is not new: Milgrom noted the coincidence a0∼cH0a_0\sim cH_0a0​∼cH0​ in 1983 [26] and has since written it as 2πa0≈cH0≈c2Λ/32\pi a_0\approx cH_0\approx c^2\sqrt{\Lambda/3}2πa0​≈cH0​≈c2Λ/3​, leaving open which of the two a0a_0a0​ is tied to [27]. The framework adds four things. It fixes the coefficient, (1−ln⁡2)/2ln⁡2(1-\ln2)/2\ln2(1−ln2)/2ln2, which observation confirms. It ties a0a_0a0​ to RΛ\RLRΛ​ rather than to H(z)H(z)H(z), so the scale does not evolve (Sec. VI). It turns the coincidence into a fixed relation, Λ=12(ln⁡2)2a02/(1−ln⁡2)2c4\Lambda = 12(\ln2)^2a_0^2/(1-\ln2)^2c^4Λ=12(ln2)2a02​/(1−ln2)2c4, from Eq. (21) and Λ=3/RΛ2\Lambda = 3/\RL^2Λ=3/RΛ2​. And it ties the same LLL to a third quantity that has nothing to do with either galaxies or cosmology: the number of qubits a quantum computer can bring into a random state. That third pin can measure LLL on its own, without GGG, and it is still to come.

The integer the quantum scale looks for, 204204204, does not depend on the quarter of a bit between log⁡2L\log_2Llog2​L and 205205205. With sss bits of entropy per ring in place of one, Eq. (15) carries sln⁡2s\ln2sln2 and log⁡2L\log_2Llog2​L falls by 12log⁡2s\tfrac12\log_2s21​log2​s, and the ceiling stays 204204204 for every sss from 0.72180.72180.7218 to 2.8872.8872.887 (Appendix A), a range that includes one nat and two bits. The ceiling is sharp on one side only. At 205205205 or more no string has room for a block of two cells for every joint outcome, so no random state can be held there. Below it the bound is soft, and by more than a unit. A block of rrr cells resolves the last qubit’s conditional probability and phase to one part in rrr. A random state whose conditional probabilities and phases are resolved that finely needs 2N−1r≤L2^{N-1}r\le L2N−1r≤L, that is N≤log⁡2(2L/r)N\le\log_2(2L/r)N≤log2​(2L/r): 202202202 for one part in 101010, 200200200 for one part in 303030, and 199199199 for one part in 100100100 (Appendix A). At 204204204 itself the blocks average L/2203=3.4L/2^{203} = 3.4L/2203=3.4 cells, so a random state is held there only coarsely, its conditional probabilities and phases rounded to the few values that blocks of three or four cells allow. We therefore expect, without deriving it (Sec. IV A), a loss of return that grows over the last few qubits below 204204204, not a wall at it. Palmer’s bit count 2N+1−2≤NL2^{N+1}-2\le NL2N+1−2≤NL [2, 4], which gives 211211211, is the weaker condition: it charges one bit for each real parameter of the state. But bits do not run out, since a string whose LLL blocks hold one cell each uses all its bits with every fraction 0 or 1; room runs out instead, two cells for each block (Sec. IV A). Eq. (3) at Palmer’s per-qubit values of LLL gives 212212212 for a quantum-dot electron and 362362362 for a hyperfine ion-trap qubit (he rounds 1010910^{109}10109 to 24002^{400}2400 and writes Nmax⁡≈400N_{\max}\approx400Nmax​≈400 [2]). Ceilings that differ by technology would restore his causal order; the same value for all would confirm ours.

That measurement also runs the chain the other way, with LLL as input and GGG as output. With LLL known, Eq. (5) gives the cell from the size of the universe, and Eq. (14) gives Newton’s constant. If the return of a random state of more than log⁡2L\log_2Llog2​L qubits falls short of the gate fidelity by more than the error of the experiment (Sec. VI), a measured ceiling NobsN_{\rm obs}Nobs​ is at most ⌊log⁡2L⌋\lfloor\log_2 L\rfloor⌊log2​L⌋. It then gives a lower bound on LLL, 2Nobs≤L2^{N_{\rm obs}}\le L2Nobs​≤L, and with Eq. (14) an upper bound on GGG. If the ceiling is where the bound itself is reached, 2Nobs≤L<2Nobs+12^{N_{\rm obs}}\le L<2^{N_{\rm obs}+1}2Nobs​≤L<2Nobs​+1, and LLL and ℓc\lcℓc​ follow to a factor of two, GGG to a factor of four. A ceiling of 204204204 then brackets GGG between 4.8×10−114.8\times10^{-11}4.8×10−11 and 1.9×10−101.9\times10^{-10}1.9×10−10 m3^33 kg−1^{-1}−1 s−2^{-2}−2, and the measured value lies inside the bracket, at log⁡2L=204.8\log_2 L = 204.8log2​L=204.8.

The universal LLL found here lies below every per-qubit value Palmer obtains from Eq. (4), so if both mechanisms were at work, the cosmological one would bind. And the coincidence he flagged is resolved. Davies’ bound [9], 1012210^{122}10122 bits for the universe, is the horizon’s count, L2/4=4.8×10122L^2/4 = 4.8\times10^{122}L2/4=4.8×10122 to leading order, whose logarithm 2log⁡2L−2=407.52\log_2L - 2 = 407.52log2​L−2=407.5 is the N≈400N\approx400N≈400 Palmer quotes for it (log⁡210122=405\log_210^{122} = 405log2​10122=405). The ceiling counts the string length LLL, not the bits of the horizon, so it is ⌊log⁡2L⌋=204\lfloor\log_2L\rfloor = 204⌊log2​L⌋=204, about half that logarithm.

VI. Predictions and Falsification

  1. A universal ceiling of at most 204 qubits in a random state, above which a random circuit and its inverse return the initial state with at most a derived fraction of the gate fidelity (Sec. IV A). It is the same for photonic, trapped-ion, superconducting, and semiconductor qubits, and insensitive to isolation. Logical error correction does not raise it: the physical strings hold the logical states too, and in the surface code the ceiling is 203203203 logical qubits (Sec. IV A). A shortfall that sets in at a different number of qubits on different technologies, with the gate fidelity accounted for, falsifies the reversal and restores Eq. (4). The test is the random circuit and its inverse of Sec. IV A, or a linear cluster state with a layer of generic rotations and its inverse, on physical qubits. Above the ceiling the state returns with at most 0.990.990.99 of the gate fidelity at 205205205 qubits, 0.790.790.79 at 206206206, 0.540.540.54 at 207207207, and 0.120.120.12 at 210210210 (Sec. IV A). At 205205205 the bound is below the resolution of any experiment; a return above the bound at 207207207 or more qubits falsifies the reversal.
  2. Newton’s constant from the ceiling. Where the shortfall above the ceiling exceeds the error of the experiment (item 1), a random state returns with the gate fidelity only at NNN with 2N≤L2^N\le L2N≤L. A measured ceiling then bounds GGG from above through G=4πc3RΛ2/(ℏL2ln⁡2)G = 4\pi c^3\RL^2/(\hbar L^2\ln2)G=4πc3RΛ2​/(ℏL2ln2), Eq. (14), and one where the bound 2N≤L2^N\le L2N≤L is itself reached gives GGG to a factor of four. A measured ceiling below 204204204 does not falsify Eq. (14), since how the return degrades below the bound is not derived (Sec. IV A).
  3. Rotation curves from baryons alone. The acceleration about a body follows Eq. (24), a function previously fitted to the data, with its scale derived: a0=(1−ln⁡2)c2/2ln⁡2 RΛa_0 = (1-\ln2)c^2/2\ln2\,\RLa0​=(1−ln2)c2/2ln2RΛ​, which is (1.200±0.011)×10−10(1.200\pm0.011)\times10^{-10}(1.200±0.011)×10−10 m s−2^{-2}−2, Eq. (25). In the deep regime rotation curves are flat, with v4=a0GMbaryonv^4 = a_0GM_{\rm baryon}v4=a0​GMbaryon​, Eq. (27), and there is no dark matter. The law for two bodies of comparable mass is not derived (Sec. IV C). A measured a0a_0a0​ that excludes 1.200×10−101.200\times10^{-10}1.200×10−10 m s−2^{-2}−2, robust detection of a dark-matter particle, or a galaxy whose rotation curve requires dark matter falsifies the galactic sector. So does an external-field effect, which a uniform field cannot produce here (Sec. IV B) and which Ref. [94] reports in rotation curves. That loses the second pin of LLL; the horizon pin, Eq. (30), the relation (29), and items 1 and 2 do not use it.
  4. The vacuum’s share, ΩΛ=ln⁡2\Omega_\Lambda = \ln2ΩΛ​=ln2. A string’s energy is on average one thermal energy of the horizon, and the strings hold all the energy inside it. The vacuum’s energy is their heat, the fraction ln⁡2\ln2ln2 of that average (Sec. IV E), so the vacuum’s share of the energy is ln⁡2=0.693\ln2 = 0.693ln2=0.693, where Planck measures 0.685±0.0070.685\pm0.0070.685±0.007 and DESI 0.7025±0.00860.7025\pm0.00860.7025±0.0086. A measurement that excludes ln⁡2\ln2ln2 beyond the correction of the strings’ interactions falsifies a premise of this share. Section IV E adds two premises to those of the sections before it: that the strings hold all the energy inside the horizon, and that their energies are spread at its temperature. With the spread would go the law of item 3, which takes its form and its scale from the spread.
  5. No redshift evolution of a0a_0a0​. The acceleration scale is tied to RΛ\RLRΛ​, not to H(z)H(z)H(z); proposals with a0∝cH(z)a_0\propto cH(z)a0​∝cH(z) predict a scale 1.81.81.8 times larger at z=1z=1z=1, and this framework predicts no change, as far back as the split of item 4 holds. With the split, Eqs. (21) and (14) give a0=(1−ln⁡2)π c7/ℏG/(ln⁡2)3/2La_0 = (1-\ln2)\sqrt\pi\,\sqrt{c^7/\hbar G}/(\ln2)^{3/2}La0​=(1−ln2)π​c7/ℏG​/(ln2)3/2L, a fixed fraction of the Planck acceleration, which changes only if GGG does, and GGG does not (item 6).
  6. Constancy of Λ\LambdaΛ. With LLL fixed, Eq. (14) gives G∝RΛ2G\propto\RL^2G∝RΛ2​ at one bit per ring (Sec. II), so the lunar-laser-ranging bound on G˙/G\dot G/GG˙/G [81] requires the horizon radius, and with it Λ\LambdaΛ, to be constant to one part in 101310^{13}1013 per year. Their product GΛ=12πc3/(ℏL2ln⁡2)G\Lambda = 12\pi c^3/(\hbar L^2\ln2)GΛ=12πc3/(ℏL2ln2), Eq. (29), is fixed by LLL alone. Since a dark-energy component with equation of state www evolves as ρ˙/ρ=−3H(1+w)\dot\rho/\rho = -3H(1+w)ρ˙​/ρ=−3H(1+w), and the expansion rate carries Λ\LambdaΛ as the term Λc2/3\Lambda c^2/3Λc2/3, the lunar bound translates, within the framework, into ∣1+w0∣≲5×10−4|1+w_0| \lesssim 5\times10^{-4}∣1+w0​∣≲5×10−4 for the drift of that term (Appendix A; twice that if the drift is referred to the density Λc4/8πG\Lambda c^4/8\pi GΛc4/8πG, which carries GGG as well). It is a translation of the lunar bound, not a prediction beyond w=−1w = -1w=−1, and it applies to the present epoch. DESI DR2 prefers evolving dark energy over a constant Λ\LambdaΛ at 2.7σ2.7\sigma2.7σ in one analysis [84] and at up to 4.2σ4.2\sigma4.2σ in another, depending on the probes combined [83]. Here w=−1w=-1w=−1 is not assumed, as it is in Λ\LambdaΛCDM. It follows from the first law and from two facts of the register: LLL and the cell are constant, and the entropy per ring stays one bit (Sec. II). With sss bits per ring, Eqs. (14) and (29) would carry sln⁡2s\ln2sln2 in place of ln⁡2\ln2ln2, so only a change in sss could change GΛG\LambdaGΛ. Every string keeps its bit (Sec. II), so in the count of free strings sss does not change. The framework therefore predicts w=−1w=-1w=−1, so the preference should not survive; a confirmed evolution of dark energy would falsify it.

VII. Conclusion

Palmer built a discrete quantum mechanics and used gravity to set its granularity. We have argued that the granularity comes first. Two postulates about cells and rings fix the number of largest rings of the register and, with the thermal state of its strings, give an observer’s horizon one bit of entropy for each. Through Jacobson’s argument, with thermodynamics and cited geometry, they give general relativity with Newton’s constant in terms of the cell. To leading order in 1/L1/L1/L the Planck length is then the cell over πln⁡2\sqrt{\pi\ln2}πln2​, and Bekenstein and Hawking’s quarter per Planck area is one bit per largest ring. Through LLL they also fix, to the same order, the product of Newton’s constant and the cosmological constant. Two measurements, GGG and Λ\LambdaΛ, fix the cell and LLL; nothing is adjusted, and every other relation of Table I is derived. Read backward, Palmer’s collapse formula gives a universal reduction clock, the de Sitter period, and mass-dependent gravitational collapse drops out. The strings’ energies are spread at the horizon’s temperature, so a string’s energy is on average one thermal energy of the horizon, and the strings’ heat is the fraction ln⁡2\ln2ln2 of that average. The strings hold all the energy inside the horizon, and the vacuum’s energy is their heat, so the vacuum’s share is predicted: ΩΛ=ln⁡2\Omega_\Lambda = \ln2ΩΛ​=ln2, 1.2σ1.2\sigma1.2σ from Planck’s value. A body’s energy is held by the strings that carry its information. From the amplitude of a string’s share and the string’s threshold, with equipartition and maximum entropy, follows the radial acceleration relation of galaxies without dark matter: a function previously fitted to the data, with its scale a0=(1−ln⁡2)c2/2ln⁡2 RΛa_0 = (1-\ln2)c^2/2\ln2\,\RLa0​=(1−ln2)c2/2ln2RΛ​ within 0.1σ0.1\sigma0.1σ of the measurements. The two scales that bear on LLL in gravity, each with the measured GGG, agree: the horizon and the galaxies give the same LLL, and since the cell cancels between them, that agreement tests the coefficient of the galactic scale.

What is not derived is stated where it arises. The law for two bodies of comparable mass is not derived (Sec. IV C); a uniform external field has no effect, so Cassini’s bound on the Sun’s quadrupole is met (Sec. IV B). Where not every string of a sphere carries the body’s information, the field equations and the bending of light are not derived (Sec. IV C). The scatter about the radial acceleration relation, the clusters, and the acoustic peaks remain open (Sec. IV C). How a largest ring closes in a universe with matter is beyond the scope of this paper (Sec. IV D). How far back the split of the strings’ energy holds is left to a later paper (Sec. IV E). The return just below the ceiling is not derived (Sec. IV A), nor is it known for which values of LLL a register exists (Sec. II). Three steps come next: the two-body law, which wide binaries test; the interactions of the strings, which the companion preprints begin [10, 35], and with them the correction to the split of the strings’ energy; and the random circuit, the one measurement of LLL that uses no gravity. Only a quantum computer can measure LLL on its own; the random circuit that can show the ceiling runs within the decade, and a return above the derived bound at 207207207 or more qubits would falsify the reversal.

Every premise the files take is a definition of one file, Sources.lean, named by its source, with the sentence of this paper it is, or a clause of the postulates carried by a structure that the file lists. The results are stated in Main.lean with those definitions as their only hypotheses, besides that LLL is not zero and that the set of a system’s configurations is not empty, and the build fails if any other hypothesis enters. The build also fails if a result takes nothing from the postulates, thermodynamics, quantum mechanics, or the cited geometry, directly or through a result derived from them. It fails as well if a result names a measured value: a decimal, a whole number above 100100100, or a constant of Numerics.lean, where the measured values stand. A result stating that a structure of the postulates exists is exempt from both checks. The results are stated in SI units, whose defining constants are constant by definition.

The named hypotheses include the thermodynamic inputs, the definition of energy (Sec. II), the Deser–Levin temperature, the gates with their fidelity, and the cited theorems of geometry that Sec. III lists. Each of those theorems has its inputs proved in the files, taken from the postulates, or stated as conditions, with the three dimensions of space as observed; no law of general relativity is taken. The clauses of the postulates enter in their words, and Postulate 1’s first sentence is a named hypothesis at each of the applications that Sec. III lists. For Sec. IV C the files count mass energy in bits, each step of the count a named hypothesis, and derive from it the amplitude of a body’s share, where one string’s bits hold the share. That a larger share has its amplitude on the same scale, Eq. (22), is a condition, which the files do not derive. Two further statements of that section are named hypotheses: the share arrives in LLL equal parts, one per tick, which add as amplitudes; and a string carries a body’s information when its global phase holds against the share, whatever its turn per tick. From these the files derive the rule by which a string carries that information, and they prove that the ticks draw the string’s phase to a phase that holds. The three steps at leading order, the count’s density, the share’s amplitude, and the carriers’ fraction, are named as such, with their errors bounded in the files.

From these the files derive the symmetry of space, G=c3kB/4ℏηG = c^3k_B/4\hbar\etaG=c3kB​/4ℏη, Einstein’s equations with matter, and the motion on geodesics of dust and of light whose energy moves with it. They also derive the cosmological constant from the space at an instant of the solution without a mass, and the Schwarzschild–de Sitter solution [73]. They prove that every largest ring has half its cells inside every observer’s horizon, that a free string holds one bit in its thermal state, and how many strings a sphere holds, on average over the drawing’s rotations. They prove that the strings’ energies, spread at the horizon’s temperature, average kBTdSk_BT_{\rm dS}kB​TdS​, with the fraction e−xe^{-x}e−x of them above x kBTdSx\,k_BT_{\rm dS}xkB​TdS​ and the vacuum’s share ln⁡2\ln2ln2, and they prove the law of Sec. IV C from its inputs, with its limits. A common acceleration of the body and of local free fall leaves the law unchanged; that a uniform external field is such an acceleration is a condition, which the files do not derive. The files prove the ceiling for strings read in step, with the counts of conditional states and the bound on the overlap of Sec. IV A. They also prove that a register with the incidence and the maps of Postulate 2 exists for every LLL with L/2−1L/2-1L/2−1 a prime power. The quadrupole of Sec. IV B is a numerical solution of the Bekenstein–Milgrom equation by the script scripts/cassini.py in the same repository, with its checks against Ref. [93]; it is not a Lean proof. The README of the repository lists every premise with the results that take it.
